definition: Mapping non-standard text — slang, misspellings, abbreviations, social-media spellings — to canonical forms.
details: Mapping non-standard text — slang, misspellings, abbreviations, social-media spellings — to canonical forms. It improves downstream NLP on noisy user-generated content.

explainer.lead: Lexical normalization maps non-standard text such as slang, misspellings, abbreviations and social-media spellings to canonical forms. It matters because noisy user-generated content otherwise degrades downstream NLP.

tiers.eli5: It is tidying up textspeak — turning 'gr8' into 'great' — before a program tries to understand the message.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it as a preprocessing step so taggers and classifiers see standard tokens on social-media input. A pitfall is over-normalising: collapsing distinctions can erase meaning or named entities.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as mapping non-standard text (slang, misspellings, abbreviations, social-media spellings) to canonical forms to improve downstream NLP on noisy content. No single mapping scheme is fixed, so normalisation targets vary by task.

explainer.example: The tweet 'gonna b l8' is normalised to 'going to be late' before sentiment analysis.
